To: data-desk-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Wellsford Road: what went wrong with our collision analysis

By Nell Garside, Western Ledger Data Desk

Our article of 2 November said that Wellsford Road had recorded 41 injury collisions between 2021 and 2025, making it Bristol’s highest-ranked road in our analysis. That figure was wrong. The correct number is 23, which places Wellsford Road sixth.

I am sorry for the alarm and confusion this caused in Fishponds. Residents questioned a figure they did not recognise, and parents have asked whether it is safe to walk their children to Wellsford Primary. They were entitled to expect better from our analysis. This was a Data Desk mistake, collectively: it is not for one person to carry.

What went wrong

To produce the ranking, we joined Department for Transport collision records to road records. That join duplicated some collision–road pairs, allowing the same accident index to appear more than once within a road’s tally. In Wellsford Road’s case, we have removed 18 duplicate entries, mostly around the Pell Street and Kingsmere Road junctions. Our revised method counts each accident index once per road.

This was an error in our processing of the data, not a revision by the DfT. A member of the Fishponds Streets Forum reconstructed the analysis from the published DfT records and could not get anywhere near 41. She was right to question our figure, and she was right about the data.

The top of the corrected table is now:

- Kingsmere Road: 32 injury collisions, previously reported as 34
- Alder Hill: 31, unchanged
- Tanner’s Way: 28, previously 29
- Crossfield Road: 26, previously 27
- Hambrook Lane: 24
- Wellsford Road: 23, previously 41

We have rerun the citywide table. No other road moves by more than two places.

The corrected article and table have been online since Friday 6 November. However, the original article has had more than 48,000 page views, so the incorrect figure travelled widely. Changing the number and adding a correction at the bottom of the page was necessary, but it was not a sufficient explanation of how an error of this size reached publication.

What the corrected figure does — and does not — mean

Twenty-three injury collisions are still 23 collisions in which someone was hurt. Three of the Wellsford Road collisions were serious, although none was fatal. The correction therefore does not mean that the road is fine, and it does not answer residents’ wider questions about road safety. It does mean that we overstated the scale of the problem and gave the road the wrong position in our ranking.

What we are changing

Any ranked Data Desk table will now be reproduced independently by a second analyst before publication. We will also publish the cleaned dataset and the analysis code alongside ranked tables, so that readers can inspect the totals and test the ranking for themselves.

I have offered to attend the Fishponds Streets Forum open meeting at Fishponds Library at 7pm on Tuesday 17 November, and to answer questions about the analysis in person.
